guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster / Gibson Les Paul / National resonator
guitar.evidence: Mark Knopfler's red Fender Stratocaster (famously used on "Money for Nothing") and Gibson Les Pauls/National resonator (for "Romeo and Juliet") are extensively documented.

tone.target: clean fingerpicked guitar with subtle compression and short room
tone.profile: clean fingerpicked guitar with subtle compression and short room
tone.summary: A warm, fingerpicked tone achieved with light compression, a clean Fender-style preamp (US Deluxe), and subtle room reverb to enhance the acoustic feel.

rig.name: Dire Straits - Romeo And Juliet - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and fingerpicking transients.
Provide subtle compression to smooth dynamics and enhance articulation.
Keep the tone clean and articulate; no distortion needed.
Simulate the warm, clean sound of a Fender-style amplifier.
Provide a bright, open sound suitable for clean fingerpicking.
Slightly boost low-mids for body and warmth without sounding muddy.
No wah effect needed for this clean, articulate tone.
Avoid pronounced chorus or heavy modulation as requested.
Add minimal echo depth to enhance the space and sustain.
blocks.gap: The request suggests keeping delay minimal or absent, so settings are kept very subtle.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle room ambiance to give the tone depth without sounding wet.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more natural, articulate fingerpicking tone.

proposals.reason: The current 'US 2x12' is too bright; a warmer, more natural cabinet will enhance the acoustic feel.
proposals.expectedGain: Warmer, rounder low-mids and better articulation.
